hypothesis: Run on the sibling branch, recorded here retrospectively. Stated as: the CDRH3 positions that contact HER2 in 1N8Z define a contact-free set large enough to reach <70% CDRH3 identity without touching the epitope.
what_we_did: Structural contact analysis at 4.5 A heavy-atom cutoff, first on 1N8Z alone (paratope_budget.py), then cross-checked across 8 trastuzumab-HER2 structures (crosscheck_structures.py, consensus_4.5.txt). Not our run: sibling task LEO/tasks/litreview-optimisation on branch LEO-litreview-optimisation, commits 9b45cdb and ae2cdef.
metrics: CDRH3 = WGGDGFYAMDY, 11 aa, positions 99-109; substitutions needed for <70% identity = 4 (4/11 = 63.6%); never-contacting positions across 8 structures = 3 (A106, M107, D108); 1N8Z-only free set = 7; CDRH3 share of interface = 26% in 1N8Z, 12-34% across structures; HER2 core epitope = 6 residues (P557, E558, P571, 585, Q602, P603) of 34 contacted in >=1 structure
learned: The 1N8Z-only answer was wrong in the optimistic direction and the cross-structure check caught it. Single-structure contact analysis called 7 CDRH3 positions free; only 3 never contact HER2 in any of 8 structures. Since 4 substitutions are needed to clear the <70% identity gate and only 3 safe positions exist, the gate CANNOT be met without mutating at least one HER2-contacting position. The identity constraint and epitope preservation are therefore in direct, quantified tension. Cheapest contacting position to sacrifice is Y109 (contacts in 1 of 8 structures), giving a defensible 4-substitution recipe: A106, M107, D108, Y109. Separately, CDRH3 carries only 20-34% of the interface, so CDRH3-only redesign (all four HER2 weights) addresses at most a third of the binding interface.
cost: 0 AMASS searches, 0 GPU; cost borne by the sibling task

hypothesis: Run by a teammate, recorded here retrospectively. Stated as: structure-based interface scores (ipTM, min_ipae, topmodel) can rank HER2 CDRH3 designs by binding.
what_we_did: Two parts. (1) Real-vs-shuffled discrimination for af3, boltz2 and chai1 on HER2 systems: real pairs (i==j) vs shuffled (i!=j), ~8,000-15,000 shuffled per model. (2) Sequence-based pre-filter on the only labelled data available (SPR-768 and FACS 524k), with single-linkage Hamming<=2 clusters held out together, results also reported on variants >=3 mutations from trastuzumab, and the 31 SPR sequences present in FACS removed before fitting. Not our run: branch origin/nick, commit aec87f4, folder NICCOLO/eda/.
inputs: SPR-768 (620 outcomes, 179 with quantified KD), FACS 524k, clonotype_split 0.7_0.15_0.15 from the Mehta data.zip
metrics: Structure scores, real-vs-shuffled AUROC: boltz2 ipTM 0.645, af3 ipTM 0.754, chai1 ipTM 0.568; topmodel score af3 0.397, boltz2 0.443, chai1 0.492 (at or below random, direction inverted); boltz2 ipTM real median 0.911 vs shuffled 0.884, and 94.3% of 8190 shuffled pairs score >=0.7. Sequence models, grouped CV: binder classifier AUROC 0.927 (0.915 at >=3 mutations), log10 KD ranker Spearman +0.687 (+0.622 at >=3 mutations), median true KD of its top 20 = 1.42 nM against 86 nM overall (~60x), recovering the 0.023 nM best binder. Per-position measured means also reported.
learned: Our ranking metric does not work on this target and a sequence model does. Boltz-2 ipTM separates real from shuffled HER2 pairs at AUROC 0.645, and 94.3% of shuffled (non-binding) pairs still score >=0.7 - so EXP-001's iptm of 0.946 and 0.965 sit squarely inside the decoy distribution and are not evidence of binding. The topmodel score is worse than random and inverted. Meanwhile a one-hot sequence model reaches Spearman +0.622 against measured log10 KD inside the >=3-mutation band we are actually allowed to design in. Consequence: rank optimisation-track designs with the sequence pre-filter, and treat refold scores as a sanity filter (discard the clearly bad) rather than a ranking. Scope limit: labels exist only for 10-residue CDRH3 variants on the trastuzumab framework, so none of this transfers to de novo designs.
cost: 0 AMASS searches, 0 GPU; cost borne by the teammate

hypothesis: Run by a teammate, recorded here retrospectively. Stated as: fold confidence (ipTM, pTM, pLDDT, min_ipae) adds screening power on top of the sequence pre-filter for trastuzumab CDRH3 variants.
what_we_did: Calibration against measured affinity rather than shuffled decoys: 60 SPR variants (30 with KD spanning 0.023-13,863 nM, 30 with no measurable KD, trastuzumab as control) folded with Boltz-2 against HER2 domain IV using the 1N8Z template, then every fold metric scored for binder/non-binder separation and for KD correlation among the 30 binders. min_ipae decoded across the CDRH3<->HER2 interface specifically. Not our run: branch origin/nick, commit 3dc1f24, files NICCOLO/eda/{make_calibration.py,p6_iptm_calib.py,p7_ipae.py,figs/iptm_calibration.csv}.
inputs: SPR-768 subset (60 variants), HER2 domain IV, 1N8Z template
metrics: AUROC for binder vs non-binder (n=60, 30/30): ipTM 0.502, pTM 0.504, pLDDT 0.356, min_ipae 0.497, mean_ipae 0.454, sequence-only p_binder 0.849. Among the 30 binders no fold metric tracks KD (all |Spearman| <= 0.21, p >= 0.28) vs sequence ranker Spearman +0.687. Adding fold metrics to sequence features made the classifier worse under grouped CV (0.849 -> 0.806). ipTM >= 0.7 passes 100% of true non-binders. ipTM spans only 0.070 because 326 of 336 tokens are identical across all 60; min_ipae has a real spread of 3.0 and still sits at chance. Fold cost measured on our H100: 7.9 s per structure (475 s for 60), against an ~80 s estimate in the Nebius docs.
learned: Stronger than EXP-003 because it calibrates against measured KD rather than shuffled decoys, and it kills the compromise position we were holding. Every fold metric is at chance, and ipTM >= 0.7 passes 100% of true non-binders, so refolding cannot even serve as a coarse gate for CDRH3 optimisation - it removes nothing. Adding fold features actively degraded the sequence classifier. The 'only 10 of 336 tokens vary' explanation does not cover min_ipae, whose spread is 3.0, so this is not a resolution artefact. Scope: fixed-framework CDRH3 optimisation only; for de novo, where the whole binder changes, AF3 ipTM retains signal (AUROC 0.75). With n=60 a strong effect (AUROC > ~0.65) is ruled out, a weak one is not. Consequence: refolding is a structural plausibility check on the handful we submit, never a screening stage.
cost: 0 AMASS searches; ~8 min H100 borne by the teammate

hypothesis: Run by a teammate, recorded here retrospectively. Stated as: a usable thermostability predictor exists for our designs, and CDRH3 redesign affects thermostability.
what_we_did: Established the Tm tooling and then tested where Tm can be moved. NanoMelt (mAbs 2025, 639 measured nanobody Tm, published held-out Pearson 0.853 / MAE 4.1 C) installed on the VM and verified to reproduce its own reference output exactly, ~45 sequences/s on the H100. Then: 41 variants of the identical 120-aa trastuzumab VH differing only in the 10-residue CDRH3; a framework-vs-CDRH3 single-point-mutation control; a full non-CDR saturation scan (1,577 single mutants, 35 s); and a 30-sequence combination test. Not our run: branch origin/nick, commits 8743169 and e542324, folder NICCOLO/thermo/.
inputs: trastuzumab VH (120 aa), SPR-768 CDRH3 variants, NanoMelt 639-measurement training data
metrics: Neither platform ships a Tm predictor: Nebius stab-ddg is StaB-ddG (binding ddG, not folding stability), Foundry AQ workflows are small-molecule tools. Cheap composition/charge/hydrophobicity features reach Pearson +0.40 / MAE 7.6 C against 8.3 C for predicting the mean. CDRH3 panel: predicted Tm spread 4.63 C (std 0.96), 0 of 40 variants beyond the 4.1 C MAE, Spearman(predicted Tm, measured KD) = +0.001. Control, single point mutations in the same VH: framework n=57 mean dTm -0.76 C (range -6.96 to +2.05, 3 beyond MAE) vs CDRH3 n=20 mean -0.09 C (range -1.30 to +0.56, 0 beyond); |dTm| median 0.63 vs 0.19 C, Mann-Whitney p=0.002. Saturation scan: mean dTm -0.59 C, 27.6% stabilising, 0 single mutant above +4.1 C, best single R98A +3.74 C, 19 below -4.1 C. Combinations strongly sub-additive: stack3 +4.28 C where additivity predicts +6.23, stack12 +1.44 C where additivity predicts +18.60; random 6-mutation subsets average +4.16 C, best +6.09 C, 12 of 29 clear +4.1 C. Sanity check: C22Q predicted -5.03 C, and NanoMelt training means are 41 C at 0 cysteines, 67 C at 2, 73 C at 4, 53 C at 5.
learned: Two decisions settled. First, the predictor question: NanoMelt is the only usable tool, it is nanobody-trained, and applying it to trastuzumab's VH shows domain artefacts (11 of the top 12 single mutations are ->Glu; V37F is a VHH hallmark position, i.e. the model partly wants to nanobody-ify the VH). So Tm is rankable in-domain for a VHH and out-of-domain for a VH or scFv. Second, and more useful for design: CDRH3 is thermostability-inert. The whole 41-variant CDRH3 spread sits inside the predictor's error bar while framework point mutations in the same VH move Tm measurably (p=0.002), so the model is not blind - CDRH3 simply does not move Tm. Spend CDRH3 entirely on affinity and epitope, and buy stability in the framework. But framework gains are small and awkward: no single mutation clears the 4.1 C error bar, stacking is sub-additive and then harmful, and the best hits are contaminated by charge bias, unpaired cysteines that abguard would reject, and position 98 immediately N-terminal to CDRH3.
cost: 0 AMASS searches; minutes of H100 borne by the teammate
